title: The Swapped Camera Lens Behind Digikala's First Web Pages
conflicts: Founding date: 1 July 2006 (Wikipedia, not cited) vs idea in spring 2006 and launch in Bahman 1385, i.e. early 2007 (the brothers to Digiato; Zoomit); story uses spring 2006 for the decision and early 2007 for the launch. Starting money: $10,000 (Forbes), 10 million toman (Zoomit), about 20 million toman (Saeed to Digiato); story gives Forbes's figure and Saeed's side by side. Hamid's 2015 'CNET and Amazon' framing (Forbes) vs his 2018 statement that Amazon was not on their radar (Digiato); story uses the later statement and avoids the comparison.
notes: Per the assignment note, sanctions appear only as attributed claims: the economist Nader Habibi via the BBC, and Saeed's own remark that not knowing how business worked abroad kept them from noticing Iran's limits. Two key sources are in Persian (Zoomit, Digiato) and are paraphrased, not quoted. Forbes is cited from an Internet Archive copy (forbes.com blocks automated requests).
